question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 26 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of auth v2.23 to ap-south likely caused the increase in p95 latency.
why_chain: auth v2.23 was deployed to ap-south 220 minutes before the change in p95 latency.
The deployment of a new version of the auth service can introduce changes that affect performance.
The increase in p95 latency is a symptom of the deployment, not the cause, but it is the most likely explanation given the timing.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in request volume in ap-south contributed to the p95 latency increase.
why_chain: The request volume in ap-south increased by 338% after the change.
Increased request volume can cause a system to become less responsive, leading to higher p95 latency.
The deployment of auth v2.23 to ap-south is the most likely cause of the increased request volume.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in error rate is a symptom of the system under stress, likely caused by the deployment.
why_chain: The error rate increased by 97% after the change.
Increased error rate is a symptom of the system under stress, which is likely caused by the deployment.
The deployment of auth v2.23 to ap-south is the most likely cause of the error rate increase.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of checkout v2.3 to eu-west caused the change in ap-south.
ruled_out.reason: checkout v2.3 was deployed to eu-west 74 minutes before the change in ap-south.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The autoscaler scaling out caused the increase in p95 latency.
ruled_out.reason: The autoscaler scaled out 20 minutes after the change in p95 latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The slow query on the auth service caused the increase in p95 latency.
ruled_out.reason: The slow query occurred 63 minutes before the change in p95 latency.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region ap-south rose from 137 ms to 298 ms (+117%), with a change point at 2026-03-26T06:10:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region ap-south: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for region ap-south rose (1236 per 5 min before, 5418 per 5 min after, +338%).
At the same time, error rate for region ap-south rose (0.41% before, 0.81% after, +97%).
Request volume 3x normal in ap-south (ap-south; 12 min after the change; record R012; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
Deployed auth v2.23 to ap-south (routine release) (auth, ap-south; 220 min before the change; record R009; fit: hours before the change, too early to explain a sudden jump)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (ap-south; 20 min after the change; record R013; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
Deployed checkout v2.3 to eu-west (routine release) (checkout, eu-west; 74 min before the change; record R010; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)
auth: WARN slow query 1.2s on report endpoint (single occurrence) (auth, us-east; 63 min before the change; record R011; fit: describes a symptom, not a change)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 220 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✗ Request volume also rose, so a traffic explanation is still open.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change

actions.action: Roll back the auth v2.23 deployment to ap-south
Monitor request volume and error rates in ap-south closely
Review and optimize the performance of the auth service
